name: DJI Mini 4 Pro
whySpecs: Records 4K/60 HDR, 4K/100 slow motion and 10-bit D-Log M at up to 150 Mbps. V30 guarantees 30 MB/s of sustained write, above what those modes need. Cards that only hit their rated speed in short bursts are what drop clips. The drone also has 2GB of internal storage, enough for about a minute of 4K if you forget the card.

faq.q: Can I use V20 cards with DJI Mini 4 Pro?
faq.a: No, use V30. DJI requires U3 (Speed Grade 3), which matches V30. A V20 card can drop frames at 4K/60 and 4K/100.

faq.q: Do I need a faster card for 4K/100 slow motion or D-Log M?
faq.a: No, a V30 card covers both. The top bitrate is 150 Mbps, about 19 MB/s. Sustained speed matters more than the label: counterfeit cards often pass a quick benchmark and then slow down during a long clip. Buy from a reputable seller and format the card in the drone.

faq.q: Which microSD brands are safest for a drone?
faq.a: SanDisk, Lexar, Samsung and Kingston all appear on DJI's recommended card lists. A card failure mid-flight loses footage you cannot reshoot.

faq.q: Can I reuse an old microSD card in my drone?
faq.a: Only if it is V30 and has never thrown an error. Worn cards fail without warning, and a failure mid-flight means lost footage.

notes: DJI officially recommends V30 cards for safe recording. Test new cards before flights.
